title: Interior of Saint Peter's, Rome
description: Panini looks down the nave at an angle, letting one immense pier cut across the view. Sunlight picks out coffers overhead while people in the aisles register as flecks of colour. The figures give the eye a human measure for the height of the vault.
note: A whole city could whisper in here. Look for the smallest visitor.

title: The Voyage of Life: Manhood
description: A voyager kneels in a little boat at the edge of a rocky channel. Behind him the last red light runs along the horizon. This is the third stage in Cole’s Voyage of Life series, where the changing character of a river gives shape to a human lifetime.
note: That patch of red on the horizon has an extraordinary amount of work to do.

title: Circe and Her Lovers in a Landscape
description: Dossi sits his enchantress at the edge of a wood. Animals gather around her as she turns toward a tablet, and the trees part to show water and distant blue hills. The calm of the landscape makes the peculiar company at her feet easy to overlook.
note: A pastoral idyll, until you start taking attendance among the animals.

title: Keelmen Heaving in Coals by Moonlight
description: Moonlight opens a pale corridor through the ships on the River Tyne. Turner sets it against several much smaller points of orange fire where the men work. Rigging and smoke nearly disappear into the sky, while the reflections carry the two sources of light into the water.
note: Two kinds of light compete for the river. The reflection gets the deciding vote.

title: Northern Landscape, Spring
description: A stretch of snow runs low across the canvas beneath an enormous blue sky. Two walkers are scarcely distinguishable against the broken ground. Friedrich gives very little space to the people who would ordinarily tell the story, leaving the weather and the empty distance to occupy the picture.
note: Spring is taking its time. The two walkers seem prepared to wait.

title: Niagara
description: Church sets the viewer close to the lip of Horseshoe Falls. The river folds from smooth green sheets into broken white water, then drops out of sight. The broad horizontal format allows the eye to follow the whole sweep of the brink before meeting the cloud of spray.
note: A landscape with the peculiar ability to make your stomach drop.

title: The Madonna of Humility
description: The Virgin sits low with the child across her lap. Two angels hold a patterned hanging behind them. The gold and the close arrangement of bodies leave little room for a surrounding world, drawing attention to the small exchange of glances at the centre of the panel.
note: The gold gets your attention. The tilt of those two heads keeps it.

title: Laocoön
description: Laocoön and his sons struggle with serpents on stony ground. The pale bodies form a chain of gestures across the foreground. El Greco sets this ancient story against a view of Toledo, visible beyond the figures beneath a sky broken into streaks of blue and grey.
note: Even the clouds seem to be trying to wriggle out of this picture.

title: The Voyage of Life: Youth
description: A young voyager reaches toward a palace formed of cloud. His boat heads along the river between flowering banks, while an angel stands ashore behind him. Cole gives the distant apparition distinct turrets and walls, making the traveller’s imagined destination almost as tangible as the trees.
note: Ambition looks particularly inviting when someone builds it a castle in the sky.

title: The Marquesa de Pontejos
description: Goya depicts the marquesa outdoors in a pale dress and a wide hat. A small dog stands at her feet. The pink ribbons and fine folds of her clothing stand out against the loose greens of the garden, while her face remains almost entirely still.
note: An astonishing dress, a remarkably composed sitter, and a dog with impeccable timing.

title: Oedipus Cursing His Son Polynices
description: Fuseli turns a family confrontation into a tightly grouped scene of reaching hands, bent knees and a fiercely extended arm. Most of the background sinks into darkness. The contrast between exposed skin, white fabric and the deep brown space makes the direction of each gesture unusually clear.
note: A family argument communicated almost entirely through elbows, wrists and a single furious finger.

title: Fog off Mount Desert
description: Church builds this coastal view from ledges of dark rock, white foam and a thin band of distant sea. The surf works its way through narrow channels in the foreground. Beyond the rocks, the haze reduces the horizon to a soft boundary between sea and sky.
note: The water is loud in the foreground. A few inches away, everything goes quiet.

title: The Adoration of the Magi
artist: Fra Angelico and Fra Filippo Lippi
description: The circular panel gathers a procession around the Holy Family. Figures wind through ruined architecture and across distant hills, carrying the eye outward from the infant. The round edge brings the movement back into the crowd, where animals, robes and gestures make a second story out of the journey.
note: One small child, an entire procession, and room left over for a peacock.

title: Lake Lucerne
credit: Gift of Richard M. Scaife and Margaret R. Battle, in Honor of the 50th Anniversary of the National Gallery of Art
description: Bierstadt places the lake between a shaded foreground and successive ranges of mountains. A patch of light catches the water, while trees near the viewer frame the distant shore. The loss of sharp detail from one ridge to the next gives the landscape its extraordinary sense of distance.
note: The farthest mountain seems a long way to travel on a piece of canvas.

title: Symphony in White, No. 1: The White Girl
description: A woman in white stands against a pale curtain, her hair a strong dark accent above the dress. A patterned rug and animal skin interrupt the white at her feet. Whistler distinguishes fabric, skin, flowers and reflected light through small differences within a narrow range of tones.
note: There are more colours hiding in this white dress than the title lets on.

title: Siegfried and the Rhine Maidens
description: A rider comes upon the Rhine maidens in a landscape of tangled branches and dark water. Ryder draws on the story of Siegfried, setting the encounter under a small patch of luminous sky. The figures emerge slowly from the same deep colours as the surrounding forest.
note: Give your eyes a moment. This forest takes its time introducing the cast.

title: The Feast of the Gods
description: Gods and goddesses gather to eat and drink in a wooded landscape. Vessels, fruit, coloured drapery and human gestures fill the lower part of the picture. Bellini and Titian’s painting gives its legendary guests the familiar habits of people who have settled in for a long afternoon.
note: Even the immortals eventually need somewhere comfortable to sit down for lunch.

title: The Adoration of the Magi
medium: tempera and oil on poplar panel
description: Botticelli places the Holy Family in an open-sided shelter amid ancient ruins. Visitors approach from both sides, gathering around the child through a chain of kneeling and standing figures. Gaps in the architecture lead into distant landscape, giving this densely attended encounter a surprising amount of open air.
note: The crowd closes in, but a sliver of blue sky keeps the whole room open.

title: The Evening of the Deluge
description: A yellow centre opens inside a sweep of darker colour. Turner lets the edges of figures and land merge into the movement of water, cloud and light. The biblical flood supplies the subject, but it takes close looking to separate the individual forms within the scene.
note: A flood painted so thoroughly that even the outlines seem to have washed away.

title: The Trojans Repairing Their Ships in Sicily
description: Trojan shipbuilders gather along the shore, with vessels drawn up near the water and buildings visible beyond. Dossi distributes the work among small groups across the foreground. Trees divide the scene into passages, so that the episode unfolds through several simultaneous tasks along the same coast.
note: Legend gives way to maintenance. Even an epic voyage needs a shipyard.

title: Pandora
description: Redon places Pandora in a narrow vertical field of soft colour and flowers. She bends her head toward the object she holds. Her blue dress gives the figure a distinct outline while the flowers and surrounding light dissolve into small, loosely connected touches of pigment.
note: The smallest gesture in a garden can have consequences well beyond the frame.

title: Self-Portrait
credit: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Robert Woods Bliss
description: Leyster turns from her easel to meet the viewer, one arm resting across the chair back. Brushes fan out from her hand. Behind her, the animated figure on the canvas provides another pose to compare with the artist’s own relaxed and carefully staged turn.
note: She has stopped work for precisely as long as it takes to catch you looking.

title: Snow in New York
description: Henri looks down a city street between dark rows of buildings. Snow reflects the narrow strip of light at the end of the street, picking out tracks, figures and wheels along the way. The rough handling keeps the surface as uneven as the winter road it describes.
note: City snow has a very short career as pure white. Henri catches what follows.

title: Saint Veronica [obverse]
description: Veronica holds up a cloth bearing the face of Christ. The white square makes a picture within the painted panel, facing the viewer directly. Behind the saint the landscape opens in stages, from the grasses near her feet to trees and blue distance beyond.
note: A portrait inside a portrait, held out as carefully as a fragile page.

title: Interior of the Pantheon, Rome
description: Panini looks across the patterned pavement of the Pantheon toward its immense coffered dome. Visitors stand, kneel and converse beneath the opening to the sky. The repeated squares in the vault grow smaller as they approach that opening, making the building’s curvature legible in a single glance.
note: Count the visitors if you like. Your eye will still end up at the oculus.

title: Mount Corcoran
description: A mountain rises above a lake bordered by trees and a low, rocky shore. Bierstadt brings the near bank into sharp detail and lets the summit stand apart in pale light. Reflections in the water extend the shapes of the shore downward into a second, quieter landscape.
note: A mountain with enough presence to command the room twice, once in reflection.

title: The Rape of Proserpine
credit: Gift of Mrs. Watson B. Dickerman
description: Turner sets the abduction of Proserpine in a wide landscape suffused with yellow light. The narrative figures occupy only a small part of the scene. Hills and trees press inward around them, shifting attention between the incident in the foreground and the luminous distance beyond.
note: The title tells you where the drama is. The light has its own opinion.

title: The Finding of Moses
description: A company of women gathers at the water’s edge around the infant Moses. Veronese arranges their varied gestures beneath the branches of a tree. Richly coloured clothes set the figures apart from one another, and a glimpse of open sky gives the dense group a backdrop.
note: A riverbank rescue dressed with all the splendour of a day at court.

title: Madonna and Child with Angels
description: Memling places the Virgin and child beneath a canopy in a space that opens onto landscape. Angels attend them on either side. Patterned textiles, slender architectural details and the distant view bring changes of scale into the small encounter at the centre of the panel.
note: A tiny world with space for an entire horizon behind its canopy.

title: Saint Martin and the Beggar
description: Saint Martin sits on a light-coloured horse beside a nearly naked beggar. The saint’s sword cuts into his cloak to divide it. El Greco stretches both figures upward in the narrow canvas, leaving a distant town and patches of ground visible around the horse’s feet.
note: An act of generosity carried by the angle of a single green cloak.

title: The Much Resounding Sea
description: Moran fills the foreground with breakers. Pale foam travels over a dark green wave and breaks apart across the surface, while the horizon remains a narrow line in the distance. The wide format draws the eye along the crest before it falls into the water below.
note: Try following one crest from end to end without imagining the sound.

title: Christ at the Sea of Galilee
artist: Circle of Jacopo Tintoretto (Probably Lambert Sustris)
description: A fishing boat pitches among steep waves, its sail and passengers leaning into the weather. On the bank, a standing figure anchors one side of the composition. The repeated diagonals of water, rigging and cloud carry the eye back and forth between shore and boat.
note: Dry land has rarely looked quite so reassuring from a few inches away.

title: Tornado in an American Forest
description: Broken trees lean across the foreground as a storm passes through a forest. Cole contrasts the dark trunks with a strip of light in the distance. Branches point in conflicting directions, allowing the force of the wind to register through the shapes it leaves behind.
note: There is no need to paint the wind when every tree is a witness.

title: Portrait of a Man with an Arrow
description: A man in a dark cap holds an arrow upright near his chest. Memling brings his hands and face close to the picture plane against a subdued ground. The feathers of the arrow provide a small, finely described counterpoint to the broad planes of his coat.
note: He gives away almost nothing. The little arrow does most of the talking.

title: The Voyage of Life: Old Age
description: The river opens into quiet water and the aged voyager sits in his boat with an angel at his side. A break in the cloud directs the eye upward. In this final painting of Cole’s Voyage of Life, the sharp rocks and rushing water have fallen behind.
note: After all those rapids, a stretch of water that scarcely moves.

title: The Return
credit: Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran, 1869)
description: An evening landscape surrounds a returning procession. Across the water and through the trees, pointed towers rise from the architecture near the centre. Cole sets the passing figures within a much larger pattern of sunlight and shadow, giving the journey a setting that appears to outlast its travellers.
note: The travellers have a destination. The evening light makes a very good case for lingering.

title: El Rio de Luz (The River of Light)
description: A river runs between wooded banks toward a luminous opening in the distance. Church describes the near leaves and branches in fine detail, then lets the farther vegetation lose definition in the haze. A reflection of the light opens a narrow vertical passage across the quiet water.
note: Follow the reflection upstream. The picture knows exactly where it wants you to look.

title: Right and Left
description: Two ducks twist above the waves, their wings held at sharply different angles. Homer brings them close enough for individual feathers to register against the cold water. The tight crop and interrupted movement hold the birds at the instant of a shot rather than in steady flight.
note: One fraction of a second, held open long enough to see every feather.

title: Green River Cliffs, Wyoming
credit: Gift of the Milligan and Thomson Families
description: Moran sets sharply lit cliffs against the low ground along the Green River. Riders and animals move across the foreground beneath bands of orange and pale rock. The horizontal sweep of the valley gives the figures room to travel while keeping their scale small beside the cliffs.
note: The riders are moving. The real procession is the light crossing the cliffs.

title: Mending the Harness
description: A horse waits on a path in a shallow landscape of muted brown and yellow. The harness gives the small scene its subject and the figures their immediate task. Ryder keeps the tonal differences slight, so that the animal’s pale coat carries much of the composition.
note: A minor roadside delay earns an entire painting. The horse appears to approve.

title: Ville-d'Avray
description: Corot looks across still water toward buildings on the opposite bank. Trees interrupt the view, their leaves and reflections softened into patches of grey and green. The far shore remains visible through gaps in the branches, so the eye moves between the foreground and the village across the pond.
note: Nothing much has to happen when the air itself has been painted this carefully.

title: A View of the Mountain Pass Called the Notch of the White Mountains (Crawford Notch)
description: A clearing leads into a mountain pass surrounded by autumn woods. Cole picks out a road and buildings at the foot of the rising ground. Light breaks across the slopes in separate patches, moving the eye from the inhabited valley toward the mountains that enclose it.
note: A road small enough to miss leads straight into a landscape too large to ignore.
